items.title: Conrad "Connie" Jones Interview, 1981-09-01
items.q: Tony did not know me from the neighborhood... he didn't know me from the neighborhood, you know, a neighborhood full of kids.

ctx.x: Well he had that mystique, he was a musician, a professional musician too. A guy that did it all the time. But we later spoke about, you know, I told him about how I used to listen to him when I was a kid and played. He couldn't even get a kick out of that. Tony was genuinely nice. He was just one of the most giving people that I've ever met in my life. He was just a warm, friendly, just a good man. And he did an awful lot for me and an awful lot for other people too. He's responsible for a lot of people being in…
Yeah. Well, Nina Piconi is really not Nina. Never Tony though, huh? No, not that I can remember. But for a long time it was Mr. El Morico. Of course, the days were different in those days.

Anyone who was older than you was Mr. and if you grew up with them, I would have been a little bit more. And if you grew up with them, it was still Mr. if somebody was 15 years older than you. It was hard making the transition from Mr. Allen to Dick or Richard. Because it just became a habit. Someone was Mr. So and so. And I never did call Jack Teagarden anything but Mr. Teagarden. Now Addie was different, because everybody called her Addie, Mrs. Tebow. But to me, you just didn't speak to a deity on a first name…

items.title: Conrad "Connie" Jones Interview, 1981-09-01
items.q: you never heard anybody called Tony pokechop?

ctx.x: What the hell, I've only got to go to work.
Yeah, well I mean, they don't care. Today's payday, so. Okay, well you get there early. Well, you never heard anybody called Tony pokechop?
